body.p: Status of the Application

According to the Advisory Action dated January 5, 2024, the previously filed amendments of November 27, 2023, were not entered. The instant Amendment amends the claims as a result of the Advisory Action based on the last entered claims as presented in Applicant's Amendment dated August 29, 2023.

By this Amendment, Claims 1 and 3-7 have been amended for clarity, and Claim 2 has been canceled without prejudice or disclaimer. No new subject matter has been added. Thus, Claims 1 and 3-7 are presently pending, with Claims 1, 6, and 7 being independent.
Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and allowance of the claims in view of the presented amendments and accompanying remarks. Claim Rejections - 35 USC § 103
Claims 1-7 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as purportedly being unpatentable over Ratnasingam (US 9,672,734), in view of Abe (US 2019/0113914), and further in view of Watanabe (US 2018/0105185).
Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections for at least the following reasons and discusses independent Claim 1 as an example.
Without any admissions, independent Claim 1 has been amended to recite features similar to those previously recited in now-cancelled dependent Claim 2:
A vehicle control device configured to control a vehicle, comprising:
an information provision device configured to provide information to a
driver of the vehicle;
a processor, during automated driving control of the vehicle, configured
to:
perform the automated driving control by automatically performing a driving operation of the vehicle relating to a driving plan of
the vehicle control device, the automated driving control comprising
operations relating to at least one of acceleration, steering, and braking,
according to the driving plan;
provide, through the information provision device to the driver, a driving event that is to occur at a point ahead in a direction of advance
from a current point, based on an automated driving plan;
judge a suitability of a driver driving operation corresponding to the driving event being performed by the driver at a point before the point
of the driving event, the driver driving operation corresponding to the
driving event being a lane change; and
provide the driver with judgment information indicating that the driver not perform the driver driving operation, based on the judging of
the suitability determining that performing the driver driving operation is
unsuitable according to the driving plan being executed by the vehicle
control device, the judgment information comprising lane change
inhibiting information indicating that a lane to be changed to is
unable to be driven on at the point before the point of the driving
event.
At a minimum, the proposed Ratnasingam-Abe-Watanabe combination do not disclose,
teach, or suggest "the judgment information comprising lane change inhibiting information
indicating that a lane to be changed to is unable to be driven on at the point before the point of the
driving event," as recited in Claim 1.
In rejecting Claim 2, the Office Action acknowledges that Ratnasingam does not teach the
cited features of Claim 1. See Office Action, p. 8. Instead, the Office Action relies on Watanabe
as allegedly disclosing these features. Applicant respectfully submits that Watanabe does not
make up for at least the above-discussed deficiencies of Ratnasingam.
Watanabe discloses constructing a driver model "in such a way that the tendency of an
operation performed by a driver for each travel environment is modeled based on information
relating to the frequency of each operation. Travel histories of a plurality of drivers are

Id. at FIG. 58C and [0555].
According to Watanabe, the action candidate determination unit "selects, as an
inexecutable action, the action in which the values (number of selected times) of the selected columns include zero." Id. at [0556].

That is, at best, Watanabe discloses that if there is a merge point ahead of a point where the driver is currently traveling, the controller of Watanabe refers to the driver's past driving history (e.g., the constructed driver model of Watanabe) to determine how far away from the merge point the driver has made many lane changes in the past when traveling on a similar road with a merge point ahead, and sets a lane change as a recommended action at the point before the merge point where the driver has made many lane changes in the past.
Furthermore, the inexecutable action of Watanabe relates to actions that have not been taken by the driver in a similar driving environment in the past.

The Office Action appears to equate the inexecutable action of Watanabe to the claimed "lane change inhibiting information." See Office Action, p. 8. Even assuming for the sake of argument only that the Office Action's equation is otherwise appropriate or correct, which Applicant does not address, Watanabe still would not disclose, teach, or suggest "the judgment information comprising lane change inhibiting information indicating that a lane to be changed to is unable to be driven on at the point before the point of the driving event," as recited in Claim 1. Instead, at best, Watanabe appears to be concerned with the driving history of the driver.
Consequently, Watanabe does not disclose, teach, or suggest at least the cited features recited in Claim 1.

The Office Action does not allege that Abe discloses the above-identified features of Claim 1 nor does Abe make up for at least these deficiencies of Ratnasingam and Watanabe. Thus, even assuming for the sake of argument only that the proposed Ratnasingam-Abe- Watanabe combination would have been proper, which Applicant does not concede, the proposed combination does not disclose, teach, or suggest all features recited in Claim 1.
In view of the above, Applicant respectfully submits that Claim 1 is patentable over the cited references and requests withdrawal of the rejection.

To the extent that independent Claims 6 and 7 recite features similar to the above-noted features of Claim 1, Applicant submits that Claims 6 and 7 are patentable for at least reasons similar to those discussed above with respect to Claim 1.

Applicant respectfully submits that dependent Claims 3-5 are patentable due to their respective dependencies, as well as for their additional features. This should not be construed as an acquiescence to Examiner's interpretation of the claims, or reading of those claim elements on the prior art, and Applicant expressly reserves the right to establish the patentability of those additional claim limitations, should the need arise. Conclusion

In view of the above, reconsideration and allowance of this application are now believed to be in order, and such actions are hereby solicited.
